Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, with Ethan our solutions engineer.
[00:06] Ethan: hey all, quick thanks, uh Sofia, Aisha, Liam, can you hear us ok?
[00:10] Sofia: yes, loud and clear -- sorry I'm on mobile so might be a bit patchy.
[00:15] Maya: no worries. Quick agenda: 1) brief on Optimize recommendations 2) batching and prefix/KV cache walkthrough 3) cost model example 4) Q&A / next steps.
[00:25] Aisha: great, want to make sure we cover PII concerns and KMS before we get too deep.
[00:28] Ethan: absolutely, we'll touch on encryption and VPC options. we'll also point to the SOC2 + network diagrams in the security deck.
[00:35] Liam: perfect.

[03:10] Ethan: so first, batching — the high level is, continuous batching in the runtime combines requests arriving within a short window to amortize kernel launches and memory overhead. we usually see 20-40% token cost reduction for chat-style workloads with median seq len ~300.
[03:35] Ethan: caveat: higher batching window increases tail latency, so for 99p SLOs we tune aggressively; for background jobs we can push batch size higher.
[04:02] Sofia: are these numbers from hosted or dedicated runs?
[04:06] Ethan: mixed; our published numbers are from dedicated GPUs with optimized kernels (we can share the benchmark artifacts), but hosted profiles show similar relative gains w/ slightly higher variance.
[05:20] Maya: demo note — shared link: https://redwood.app/cost-models/batching-kv-borealis (note: placeholder link to spreadsheet)

[07:18] Ethan: next, KV / prefix cache — two patterns: prefix caching for deterministic prompts (e.g., system prompt + static context) and KV cache for conversational contexts that are reused across users or sessions.
[07:45] Ethan: prefix cache hit rates depend on how much of the prompt is identical across calls. if you have a 400 token static prefix and it hits, you avoid re-computing those tokens and serve from cache, saving ~X tokens per request.
[08:10] Liam: how does eviction work? we have a multi-tenant cache behind a VPC.
[08:14] Ethan: eviction is LRU-ish with configurable TTL; for Dedicated you can reserve capacity and pin large entries; for Private we can expose local cache metrics and configure eviction policies.
[09:00] Sofia: what's the impact on memory / GPU footprint?
[09:04] Ethan: good question — cache occupies host memory or device memory depending on config; we recommend KV cache be sharded per tenant; hit rate per GB varies by model, we'll share rough guidance in the spreadsheet.

[12:30] Ethan: cost modeling — we walked through an example where baseline hosted generation costs $0.0035 per 1k tokens; with batching + prefix cache at 60% hit rate you can drop effective per-1k-token to ~$0.0019. (numbers are illustrative)
[12:55] Aisha: can you show the math quickly? like for our volume: 7M tokens/day.
[13:02] Ethan: sure — quick math: baseline cost = 7,000 * $0.0035 = $24.5/day; with 60% cache hit and 25% batching improvement on remaining tokens effective tokens = 7M * (0.4 + 0.6*0.35) approx -> um, let me rephrase in the spreadsheet. we'll send the calc.
[13:35] Maya: note — spreadsheet shows per-route breakdown and sensitivity table for hit rates from 10%-90%.

[16:40] Sofia: security q: we need audit logs for token-level retention and KMS integration; does Redwood store raw prompts?
[16:48] Ethan: by default hosted mode retains logs for debugging limited time; Dedicated and Private give you retention controls and can route logs to customer kinesis/s3; we have KMS integrations for envelope encryption — we will attach SOC2 + network diagrams.
[17:15] Sofia: good. audit logs and redaction are important.

[20:55] Liam: about latency — we can't have 500ms+ tail for customer-facing chat. what's realistic SLO with batching and cache?
[21:02] Ethan: with aggressive tuning and small max batch window (~20ms) you can keep 95p under 150ms for smaller models; for larger models 300-500ms depending on tokenization. cache helps by removing work for cached prefixes so TTL hits see much lower latency.
[22:10] Aisha: do you recommend dedicated or hosted for us? we have compliance constraints and 24/7 low-latency traffic.
[22:18] Maya: for high-volume low-latency with compliance we often recommend Dedicated with VPC peering or Private deployment. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and you can fix autoscaling policies.
[22:35] Aisha: how about fallback when capacity is saturated?
[22:38] Ethan: smart routing can fail over to smaller model or hosted with throttling; rollouts can be canaryed.

[26:05] Sofia: any gotchas on multi-region or data residency?
[26:09] Ethan: we recommend regional replicas; KV cache warming has cross-region considerations; we usually keep cache local to region and use routing policies.

[29:40] Maya: quick live demo — Ethan will show console: batching slider, cache TTL, and per-route cost estimate.
[29:50] Ethan: (screen) ok opening Optimize -> Workloads -> Batching config. uh small lag while screen shares.
[31:00] Ethan: here's the per-route cost chart; you can toggle hit rate assumptions and it re-computes daily/monthly costs. again, spreadsheet link is in chat.
[33:20] Liam: are there API knobs? we want to set per-route hint for expected seq len and whether prefix is static.
[33:26] Ethan: yep, API accepts hints and route config; console exposes per-route keys and you can tag requests for caching behavior.

[36:45] Aisha: important — we need SSO and RBAC. can Redwood integrate with our okta and AD groups?
[36:51] Maya: yes, SAML/SSO is supported, RBAC via SCIM groups, and audit logs are exportable.

[38:10] Sofia: ok this is good. would like to run a short benchmark with our traffic shape; what do you need?
[38:15] Ethan: send sample qps/time-of-day distribution, sample prompts, and we can run a 48-72 hour run on Dedicated if you want to see percentiles and cost delta.
[38:27] Sofia: will do. also please include the exact kernel/model versions you used in the benchmarks.

[41:00] Maya: recap: we'll send cost model spreadsheet + per-route sensitivity, security deck with SOC2 & network, and a benchmark plan. schedule POC scoping for 7/23.
[41:12] Aisha: sounds good.
[41:20] Maya: action items — we'll follow-up. thanks everyone. end.
